runoff_source.field: P-E from the forcing climatology, not mrro
runoff_source.why: the run's global water budget closes to 0.03% of the mean and the land surplus matches the sea deficit, but mrro accounts for only 15% of that surplus

water_balance.read_against: the larger of the basin's own capacity and what passed through it in the year

periodic_steady_state.crossing_note: closed-basin lake area only. A floodplain's inundated area needs a height-above-nearest-drainage distribution and a routing model that do not exist here, and a seasonally saturated soil is a water content rather than an area. Neither is merged into this.
periodic_steady_state.what_carries_a_season: residence time, and the product is per basin because of it: a deep terminal lake holds years of supply and its surface barely moves inside one, while a shallow playa's area is almost all seasonal
periodic_steady_state.omission: the catchment's delivery is flat through the cycle. Only the lake's own surface fluxes carry a season here; land_water_ledger.yaml declares that as seasonal_phase_of_catchment_delivery

open_water_evaporation.method: Penman combination, water albedo and roughness, NOT floored at the model's land rate; shared with carve_verdict.py
open_water_evaporation.validation: ratio over ocean cells, which already are open water; the only place the estimate can be checked
open_water_evaporation.what_the_lake_solves_are_forced_with: the bin-weighted mean of the per-bin evaluation, over the basin sinks; the annual-mean evaluation is not used

evaporation_interval_bracket.what_it_is: the interval the open-water evaporation estimate is evaluated over, which is not the same question as which estimator to use
evaporation_interval_bracket.missing_term: seasonal heat storage in the water body, which needs a lake depth and a mixed-layer model this project does not have. Declared rather than estimated
evaporation_interval_bracket.which_end_is_used_here: the bin mean, matching the carve verdict's primary bound. The spread is the number to read, not a second answer
